policy.name: None in force with fiscal MSME incentives (Chandigarh Industrial Policy 2015 is facilitation-oriented; new Chandigarh Industrial Policy under drafting since July 2026)

other_benefits: Chandigarh Industrial Policy 2015: single-window/time-bound services, 20% procurement preference for local MSEs - no capital/interest/SGST/ED incentives reported (press, 2015)
Chandigarh Startup Policy 2025 notified 29-04-2025 (startups only; Rs 10 crore annual corpus) - not an MSME manufacturing incentive

Rental subsidy scheme and interest subvention scheme for MSMEs (MSME Financing Campaign) were 'finalised' and expected to be notified by 31-05-2026 (Tribune, 28-05-2026); no notification or figures found

Proposed in the new draft industrial policy (Tribune, 27-07-2026): partial reimbursement of certification/testing/export-licence costs for units spending up to Rs 10 lakh; possible concessions on electricity charges and statutory levies - not notified
unverifiable: No current UT Chandigarh industrial/MSME policy with computable fiscal incentives (capital subsidy, SGST, interest, electricity duty, power tariff, certification) could be found as of 17-10-2026.

chandigarh.gov.in and the UT Industries Department site were unreachable from this environment, so the status of the rental-subsidy and interest-subvention schemes (due by 31-05-2026) could not be checked against an official notification.
Chandigarh units may access central schemes only (e.g. PMEGP, CGTMSE, ZED, DGFT export interest subvention) - not covered here.
